'''Phosani's Nightmare''' is a more difficult version of [[The Nightmare]], encountered by selecting ''Drink-from'' on the [[Pool of Nightmares]] in the [[Sisterhood Sanctuary]]. 

Phosani's Nightmare can only be fought alone, and the game encourages the player to have at least one normal Nightmare kill before attempting Phosani's Nightmare; trying to attempt the boss without any Nightmare kill count will result in an initial warning advising the player to do so, though they may ignore it and proceed to the boss fight.

Compared to fighting the Nightmare solo, Phosani's Nightmare is significantly faster, with little damage being taken if players master the fight's mechanics, though far more punishing when mistakes are made. Although the boss itself has a lower drop rate for uniques compared to the original, it makes up for it with its faster kill times and increased quantities of normal drops.{{CiteNews|url=https://secure.runescape.com/m=news/phosanis-nightmare-poll-blog?oldschool=1|title=Phosani's Nightmare: Poll Blog|newsdate=10 May 2021|quote=}} It also possesses two unique drops the original lacks; the [[Slepey tablet]], which allows players to access the Nightmare even quicker, and the [[parasitic egg]], an item that unlocks a cosmetic skin for the [[Little Nightmare]].

==Difference in mechanics==
{{See also|Phosani's Nightmare/Strategies}}
There are notable differences in mechanics compared to the regular Nightmare encounter:
* Standard attacks hit significantly higher, but successfully praying against them will fully block the attack.
* Special attacks and minions are stronger and some are used in combination with one another: for example, spores are always summoned before six consecutive claw attacks.
** Phosani's Nightmare will use multiple consecutive claw attacks in conjunction with Flower Power or Spores.
** The spores slow the player's attack speed by 2 ticks instead of 1 (doubled if maging), and they also drain 6 prayer points every time the player yawns.
* Crush weapons will always deal their maximum hit against [[Husk (Phosani's Nightmare)|husks]] and weakened [[Parasite (Phosani's Nightmare)|parasites]].
* There are four phases instead of three: 3 phases of 400 shield durability and 1 phase of 150 health, along with 3 sets of totems (12 in total) with 200 charge. In total, the player has to deal 1,350 physical damage and 1,200 charge damage (using magic) for a total of 2,550 damage in Phosani's encounter. The original fight, in comparison, requires 7,800 damage (3 phases each of 2,000 shield durability and 600 charge damage (using magic)), making kills ~3x faster on average.
* After each phase, the number of sleepwalkers spawned increases by one, capping at 4 at the end of the third phase, whereas the original fight has sleepwalkers scale to the amount of players present (still 1 for solo).
* Phases 1-3 use a set rotation of specials taken from the original encounter.
* In phase 3, Phosani's Nightmare will deactivate the player's protection prayer if they had already had the prayer active before the attack. She also has an increased chance of attacking with melee.
* In phase 4, the "desperation phase", she indefinitely performs Grasping Claws and summons sleepwalkers until killed. One sleepwalker is summoned at a time; should they reach her, she will unleash a blast causing 15 damage.

==Development history==
Phosani's Nightmare was {{UD|Phosani's Nightmare and Tinted Hitsplats|initially released}} as a competition lasting one week from 5 March 2020, allowing players to win free membership and signed artwork. Like the currently existing Phosani's Nightmare, it had more punishing mechanics and could only be fought solo, although it did not have reduced health, reduced damage when fought correctly, or phase randomisation. Its loot table was unchanged from the regular encounter.

*Its standard magic and ranged attacks could hit up to 90, while its slashing attack could hit up to 115.
*The Grasping Claws and Surge attack would instantly kill the player if hit.
*The spores would slow attack speed by 2 ticks, and last longer.
*Two sleepwalkers spawned instead of one.
*The husks were much more accurate and dealt more damage.
*Parasites could heal Phosani's Nightmare over 100 health, even when weakened. In addition, the damage taken when it burst out was 10 instead of 5, even when weakened.
*The Curse attack shuffled the protection prayers by one to the left rather than the right: clicking on Protect from Magic activated Protect from Melee, Protect from Missiles activated Protect from Magic and Protect from Melee activated Protect from Missiles.

The encounter was later offered in a [[Update:Phosani's Nightmare: Poll Blog|poll blog]] on 4 May 2021, as a piece of end-game content that would take less development time to create than a brand new boss. The boss was then polled in [[Poll:Phosani's Nightmare Poll|Phosani's Nightmare Poll]] and passed with 89.1% support.

==Trivia==
*Phosani's Nightmare's examine text is a reference to the song ''{{WP|Sweet Dreams (Are Made of This)}}'' by British pop duo {{WP|Eurythmics}}.
*Phosani's Nightmare had a festive override wearing a [[red partyhat]] during the [[2021 Christmas event/Gallery|2021]], [[2022 Christmas event/Gallery|2022]], [[2023 Christmas event/Gallery|2023]], [[2024 Christmas event/Gallery|2024]], and [[2025 Christmas event/Gallery|2025]] Christmas events.
